name: Rocket salad
grown_as: Salad rocket, an annual sown in rows and picked young for its peppery leaves (William's records list it as Eruca sativa, the older name).
habit: A loose rosette 15 to 25 cm high when picked. It bolts quickly in summer into an upright branched stem 40 to 80 cm with flowers at the top.

leaf.arrangement: A rosette; alternate on the flowering stem
leaf.type: Simple but deeply lobed, like a lyre: a large end lobe and smaller side lobes
leaf.outline: Oblong, 8 to 15 cm long; a large rounded to oval end lobe and two to five pairs of smaller, oblong side lobes with gaps between them, getting smaller towards the base
leaf.base: Narrowing into a short stalk, the smallest lobes running down it
leaf.tip: The end lobe rounded and blunt
leaf.margin: The lobes smooth or with a few blunt shallow teeth
leaf.veins: A pale midrib, a side vein running into each lobe
leaf.surface: Smooth, slightly fleshy, hairless or with a few scattered bristles
leaf.stalk: Short, pale, merging into the lobed blade

flower.form: A cross-shaped flower of four petals
flower.petals: Four, free, oval to spoon-shaped with a long narrow claw, the outer part spreading
flower.colour: Cream to pale yellowish white with clear dark purple-brown veins running along each petal
flower.centre: Six stamens with yellow-cream anthers, close round a green style
flower.behind: Four narrow upright sepals, green tinged purple, hugging the petal claws
flower.carried: In loose spikes at the tips of the stems, opening from the bottom up, the spike lengthening as it flowers

fruit: Upright pods 1.5 to 2.5 cm held close against the stem, plump and cylindrical, ending in a flat, sword-shaped beak about a third of the pod's length. Green, drying straw-brown, with two rows of small seeds. Seeds oval and slightly flattened, 1.5 to 2 mm, pale yellow-brown.
seedling: Two kidney-shaped seed leaves on short stalks, broader than long with a notch at the tip, like a heart with the stalk at its point, then oval true leaves with wavy edges; the lobes come on later leaves.
winter: Nothing: an annual, though autumn sowings carry on under cover.

leaf: a large rounded end lobe and smaller oblong side lobes in pairs, gaps between them
the side lobes getting smaller towards the base
a pale midrib, smooth or bluntly toothed lobes
bloom: four cream petals in a cross
dark purple veins along each petal
seed: small oval slightly flattened seed 1.5 to 2 mm
seedling: two kidney-shaped seed leaves notched at the tip
the first true leaf oval and wavy, not yet lobed
young: a loose rosette of lobed leaves, large end lobes
crop: a loose rosette of lyre-shaped lobed leaves 8 to 15 cm
flower: an upright branched stem with lobed leaves
cream purple-veined four-petalled flowers in loose spikes at the top
seedhead: short plump pods pressed upright against the stem
each pod with a flat beak at its tip

look_alikes: Wild rocket (Diplotaxis tenuifolia) is a perennial with narrower, more deeply cut leaves, bright yellow flowers and long flat pods without the broad beak. White mustard and charlock have yellow flowers and bristly leaves. Radish leaves are rough and hairy with purple-veined white or mauve flowers.
